listenings.text: Hi, I'm Mike, and I live in Queens, one of the five boroughs of New York. Last weekend my sister came from Ohio, so I was a tour guide for two days. On Saturday we took the subway to Manhattan. We went to the Metropolitan Museum in the morning. It was very crowded, and we waited in line for thirty minutes. In the afternoon we ate hot dogs in Central Park. On Sunday we didn't go to Manhattan. We went to Brooklyn, and we saw the skyline from the water. My sister wanted to see a Broadway show, but the show sold out, so we saw stand-up comedy in a small club. She loved it.

Hello, my name is Giulia, and I am from Milan. In September I went to New York for the first time. I didn't have a ticket for a Broadway show, and all the big shows sold out. So one afternoon I went to the ticket booth in Times Square. I waited in line for almost an hour, but I got a ticket for the same night, and it was half the price. The show was a musical. I didn't understand all the words, because they sang very fast, but the music was fantastic. After the show I took the subway back to the hotel. It was midnight, and the train was full.

reading.rtitle: Ten Days in New York With a Small Budget
paras: Last October, travel writer Ana Costa spent ten days in New York. She wanted to see the city, but she didn’t want to spend a lot of money. Her first decision was simple: no taxis. She bought a subway card on the first day and took the subway everywhere. It was fast and cheap, and she saw a different borough almost every day.

Museums were her second secret. Many museums in New York have free admission on some evenings, so Ana went to three of them for free. She waited in line for forty minutes at one museum, but she didn’t mind. Inside, it was quiet and beautiful. On a free evening she also walked across the Brooklyn Bridge and saw the skyline at sunset.

Did she see a Broadway show? Yes, she did. The famous shows sold out weeks before, so she went to the ticket booth in Times Square and got a cheap ticket for the same night. On her last night, she went to a small club for stand-up comedy. She didn’t understand every joke, she says, but she laughed a lot. Her advice: plan the free things first, and leave some money for one special night.
